Man Steals Car, Rams Police Vehicle, Jumps Into Water, AirTag Gives Him No Chance
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
If you need more proof that AirTags have become a must-have anti-theft hardware for car owners, here’s a recent case from North Seattle.
A 38-year-old thief stole an SUV, drove away in seconds, and hoped to escape without being caught without even thinking that every move he made was being followed. An AirTag planted in the vehicle he stole revealed his location allowing the police to rapidly track him down.
The incident happened last week when the SUV owner was just unloading stuff from his car. The thief got into the car through the open tailgate when the owner wasn’t around and pressed the start engine button. Because the owner was nearby, the engine started, so he drove away in just a few seconds.
The owner immediately called 911 and told the police officer who arrived at the scene that an AirTag had been planted into the vehicle. It turns out the AirTag was actively broadcasting its location, meaning there’s a good chance that the thief had an iPhone in his pocket.
AirTags are small, pill-shaped devices that use Bluetooth to connect to nearby Apple devices to use their Internet connection specifically to transmit their locations. They do this through the Find My network, and owners can just fire up the Find My app on their iPhones, iPads, or MacBooks to see the location on the map. AirTags don’t come with a power-off button, and the only way to turn off these trackers is to remove the battery.
AirTags use CR2032 batteries, meaning they don’t need to be recharged. They should last up to several months per every battery.
The SUV owner jumped into the patrol car and provided the officer with the location information offered by the AirTag. In just a few minutes, the officer located the car and approached it. The thief was still inside, and after going in reverse and ramming the police car, he managed to jump outside to run away on foot.
He ended up jumping into Lake Washington, trying to swim away. After realizing he was surrounded only by cold water and police officers - apparently , the thief needed 25 minutes to do this - he decided to get out of the water and surrender to the police. He still didn’t give up, as he provided the police with a fake name. The reason was simple: he had several active warrants.
He was taken into custody and is now facing multiple chargers, including stealing the SUV.
AirTags have once again helped recover a stolen car, and despite the damage caused by the thief, it’s pretty clear that such trackers can come in very handy when the worst happens. If you need advice on where to install an AirTag, here are the best 5 places in your cabin .
